evidence.source: 甘木, “說字（九則）,” Fudan University Center for Excavated Texts and Paleography
evidence.text: The author rejects the familiar hand-rubbing-wheat analysis and argues from Western Zhou inscription forms for more than one graphic analysis: one proposed shape relates to bundled fuel and possibly 㷢; a distinct form is interpreted as misaligned hands, with 左 added as a phonetic note. The article describes these as argued analyses, not a single established linear history.
evidence.title: 甘木：說字（九則）

evidence.source: 漢典 (Zdic), citing 《說文解字》 and 段玉裁’s 《說文解字注》
evidence.field: 差 說文解字 and annotation
evidence.text: The received Shuowen account glosses 差 as mismatch and analyzes it as 从左从𠂹; it also records a Zhou-script form from 二. Duan Yucai discusses mismatch and divergent forms, and relates some uses to selection. This is a historical lexicographic account, not direct confirmation of the earliest graph.
evidence.title: 差 chà、chā、chāi、cī - 漢典

evidence.text: The file description identifies the image as a modern SVG rendering of 差 in a Western Zhou bronze-script style, citing Hanziyuan image 31.F03B and identifying 同簋蓋 (mid-Western Zhou) as the source context. The page states public-domain status for the SVG representation. This is a redrawing, not an artifact photograph.

search_audit.outcome: Opened and inspected Han Dian, including its Shuowen and Duan Yucai accounts, reading information, and named inscription examples.

gaps: The Commons description page could not be opened directly by the web tool. Its search result exposed source, date-context, image type, and reuse claims; no image pixels were inspected.

No independently verified direct upload image URL was obtained. The candidate image URL below is derived from the Commons file naming scheme, while the page metadata and rights were inspected via search results.

The file identifies a particular Western Zhou bronze-script style and points to an image associated with 同簋蓋, but it is a modern vector redraw and cannot stand alone as evidence for disputed component analyses.
The Fudan article argues against the wheat-rubbing explanation; the current graph’s resemblance to 羊 or an interpretation involving 來 should not be presented as established history.

items.period: Mid-Western Zhou (file description associates source context with 同簋蓋)
items.tradition: Western Zhou bronze-script style; modern SVG redraw
items.caption: A modern redraw of a 差 form catalogued in Western Zhou bronze-script style. Its identification comes from the Commons description, which cites an 同簋蓋 form; graphic interpretation remains debated.
items.alt: Single dark bronze-script-style 差 glyph centered on a light background, rendered as a clean vector drawing.
items.selection_reason: One well-provenanced candidate gives an example of the Western Zhou form tradition discussed in the paleographic article and has a described reusable license. It is explicitly a redraw, not an artifact photograph.
items.rights: Public domain, as stated for the modern SVG representation on its Commons description page.

limitations.text: The proposed image is a modern SVG redrawing. Neither the image pixels nor the underlying inscription rubbing were independently inspected in this research step.
The candidate illustrates a catalogued bronze-script form but does not settle whether the graph derives from rubbing wheat, bundled fuel, misaligned hands, or another proposed analysis.
